title: Phishing
question: What is phishing and what do attackers try to get from people?
key_facts: Phishing is a form of social engineering and a scam.
In phishing, attackers deceive people into revealing sensitive information.
Phishing can be used to steal credentials or to install malware.

title: Multi-factor authentication
question: What is two-factor authentication and why is it useful?
key_facts: Two-factor authentication is also called multi-factor authentication.
The user must present two or more distinct types of evidence to gain access.
It protects personal data from being accessed by an unauthorized third party.

title: Ransomware
question: What is ransomware and how does it harm victims?
key_facts: Ransomware is a type of malware.
Ransomware holds the private data of a victim hostage until a ransom is paid.
Ransomware can encrypt the victim's data.

title: Malware
question: What is malware?
key_facts: Malware is short for malicious software.
Malware is software intentionally designed to cause disruption or damage to computers or networks.
Computer viruses, worms and Trojan horses are types of malware.

title: Identity theft
question: What is identity theft?
key_facts: Identity theft occurs when someone uses another person's personal identifying information without permission.
Identity theft is used to commit fraud or other crimes.
Information such as a name, identifying number or credit card number can be misused.

title: Cyberbullying
question: What is cyberbullying and who is most affected by it?
key_facts: Cyberbullying is bullying or harassment using electronic means.
Cyberbullying is common among teenagers and adolescents.
The growth of cyberbullying is linked to young people's use of social media.

title: Password strength
question: What makes a password strong?
key_facts: Password strength measures how well a password resists guessing or brute-force attacks.
The strength of a password depends on its length, complexity and unpredictability.
Strong passwords lower the risk of a security breach.

title: Advance-fee scam
question: What is an advance-fee scam?
key_facts: An advance-fee scam is a form of fraud.
The victim is promised a large sum of money in return for a small upfront payment.
After payment, the fraudster asks for more fees or disappears.

title: Scholarship
question: What is a scholarship and do students have to pay it back?
key_facts: A scholarship is a form of financial aid awarded to students for education.
Scholarships are awarded based on criteria such as academic merit or financial need.
Scholarship recipients are not required to repay scholarships.

title: Distance education
question: What is distance education?
key_facts: Distance education is also known as distance learning.
In distance education the learner and the teacher are separated in time or distance.
Distance education today usually involves online learning.

title: Literacy
question: What does literacy mean?
key_facts: Literacy is traditionally the ability to read and write.
Literacy is also used more broadly to include understanding and using written information.
Literacy enables individuals to participate effectively in society.

title: Vocational education
question: What is vocational education?
key_facts: Vocational education prepares people for a skilled craft or occupation.
Vocational education is also called technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
Vocational education is known by different names in different countries.

title: Student loan
question: What is a student loan and what can it be used for?
key_facts: A student loan is a loan designed to help students pay for higher education.
Student loans can cover tuition, books and living expenses.
Repayment of a student loan may be deferred while the student is still in school.

title: Compulsory education
question: What is compulsory education?
key_facts: Compulsory education is a period of education required of all people.
Compulsory education is imposed by the government.
Under compulsory schooling, parents are obliged to send their children to school.

title: Bachelor's degree
question: What is a bachelor's degree and how long does it take?
key_facts: A bachelor's degree is an undergraduate degree awarded by higher education institutions.
A bachelor's degree takes three to six years of study.
The most common bachelor's degrees are the Bachelor of Arts and the Bachelor of Science.

title: Homeschooling
question: What is homeschooling and who usually teaches the children?
key_facts: Homeschooling is the education of school-aged children outside a traditional school.
Homeschooling is also known as home education.
Homeschooling is usually conducted by a parent, a tutor or an online teacher.

title: Minimum wage
question: What is a minimum wage?
key_facts: A minimum wage is the lowest pay that employers can legally pay their employees.
Most countries had introduced minimum wage laws by the end of the 20th century.
Minimum wage policies vary between countries.

title: Unemployment benefits
question: What are unemployment benefits and who can receive them?
key_facts: Unemployment benefits are payments made by governmental bodies to unemployed people.
Unemployment benefits are also called unemployment insurance.
Benefits are generally given to people who became unemployed through no fault of their own.

title: Trade union
question: What is a trade union and what does it do for workers?
key_facts: A trade union is an organization of workers.
A trade union aims to maintain or improve the conditions of employment of its members.
Trade unions seek better wages, benefits and working conditions.

title: Résumé
question: What is a résumé and what should it contain?
key_facts: A résumé is a document used to present a person's background, skills and accomplishments.
Résumés are most often used to apply for a job.
A typical résumé contains a summary of relevant job experience and education.

title: Employment contract
question: What is an employment contract?
key_facts: An employment contract is a contract between an employee and an employer.
An employment contract sets out rights and responsibilities between the parties.
Under an employment contract the employer agrees to pay the employee a wage.

title: Child labour
question: What is child labour?
key_facts: Child labour is work that interferes with children's ability to attend school.
Child labour is work that is mentally, physically, socially or morally harmful to children.
Child labour is prohibited by legislation worldwide.

title: Occupational safety and health
question: What is occupational safety and health?
key_facts: Occupational safety and health is concerned with the safety, health and welfare of people at work.
Occupational safety and health is a multidisciplinary field.
Occupational safety and health is also known as occupational health and safety.

title: Pension
question: What is a pension?
key_facts: A pension is a fund into which amounts are paid during a person's working career.
A pension makes periodic payments to support a person's retirement.
A pension may be a defined benefit plan or a defined contribution plan.

title: Passport
question: What is a passport and what is it used for?
key_facts: A passport is a travel document issued by a government.
A passport certifies a person's identity and nationality.
A passport is used for international travel.

title: Birth certificate
question: What is a birth certificate?
key_facts: A birth certificate is a vital record.
A birth certificate documents the birth of a person.
A birth certificate can be a certified copy of the registration of a birth.

title: Vaccination
question: What is vaccination and how does it protect people?
key_facts: Vaccination is the administration of a vaccine.
Vaccination helps the immune system develop immunity to a disease.
When enough of a population is vaccinated, herd immunity results.

title: Identity document
question: What is an identity document?
key_facts: An identity document is a document proving a person's identity.
An identity document in the form of a plastic card is called an identity card.
In some countries identity documents are compulsory.

title: Welfare spending
question: What is social welfare support from the government?
key_facts: Welfare is government support for members of a society.
Welfare helps people meet basic needs such as food and shelter.
Social insurance programs support people who have previously contributed, such as through pensions.

title: Universal health care
question: What is universal health care?
key_facts: Universal health care is a health care system in which all citizens have some level of health coverage.
Universal health care is also called universal health coverage.
Universal health coverage can be achieved through many different models.

title: Voter registration
question: What is voter registration?
key_facts: Voter registration is the requirement to register on an electoral roll.
Registration is usually a prerequisite for being permitted to vote.
The rules for voter registration vary between jurisdictions.

title: Income tax
question: What is income tax?
key_facts: Income tax is a tax imposed on individuals or entities.
Income tax is levied on the income or profits earned.
Income tax rates may increase as taxable income increases.
